statement:
Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
An object of $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ is a triple $(N,M',\varphi)$, where $N$ is a $B$-module, $M'$ is an $A'$-module, and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'}A=M'/IM'$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.
Let $G:\mathrm{Mod}_{B'}\to\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ send $L'$ to $(L'\otimes_{B'}B,L'\otimes_{B'}A',\mathrm{can})$, with $\mathrm{can}$ the canonical identification after tensoring both components with $A$.
The functor $F:(N,M',\varphi)\mapsto N\times_{\varphi,M}M'$ is right adjoint to $G$. Moreover $G\circ F$ is canonically isomorphic to the identity on $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$: for every compatible triple, $N'\otimes_{B'}B\cong N$ and $N'\otimes_{B'}A'\cong M'$, compatibly with $\varphi$.

Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.

Let $G:\mathrm{Mod}_{B'}\to\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ send $L'$ to $(L'\otimes_{B'}B,L'\otimes_{B'}A',\mathrm{can})$, with $\mathrm{can}$ the canonical identification after tensoring both components with $A$.
conclusions: $F:(N,M',\varphi)\mapsto N\times_{\varphi,M}M'$ is right adjoint to $G$; the canonical maps $N'\otimes_{B'}B\to N$ and $N'\otimes_{B'}A'\to M'$ identify $G(F(N,M',\varphi))$ with $(N,M',\varphi)$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-module-over-fibre-product}
In Situation \ref{situation-module-over-fibre-product}
the functor (\ref{equation-functor}) has a right adjoint, namely
the functor
$$
F : (N, M', \varphi) \longmapsto N \times_{\varphi, M} M'
$$
where $M = M'/IM'$. Moreover, the composition of $F$ with
(\ref{equation-functor}) is the identity functor on
$\text{Mod}_B \times_{\text{Mod}_A} \text{Mod}_{A'}$. In other words,
setting $N' = N \times_{\varphi, M} M'$ we have
$N' \otimes_{B'} B = N$ and $N' \otimes_{B'} A' = M'$.

statement:
Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
An object of $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ is a triple $(N,M',\varphi)$, where $N$ is a $B$-module, $M'$ is an $A'$-module, and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'}A=M'/IM'$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.
Let $(f_N,f_{M'}):(N_1,M'_1,\varphi_1)\to(N_2,M'_2,\varphi_2)$ be a morphism of compatible triples, so the two component maps commute with the isomorphisms after extension of scalars to $A$. If $f_N:N_1\to N_2$ and $f_{M'}:M'_1\to M'_2$ are surjective, then the induced $B'$-linear map $N_1\times_{\varphi_1,M_1}M'_1\to N_2\times_{\varphi_2,M_2}M'_2$, where $M_i=M'_i/IM'_i$, is surjective.
hypotheses: Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.

An object of $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ is a triple $(N,M',\varphi)$, where $N$ is a $B$-module, $M'$ is an $A'$-module, and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'}A=M'/IM'$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.
A morphism of such triples $(N_1,M'_1,\varphi_1)\to(N_2,M'_2,\varphi_2)$ has surjective $B$-module and $A'$-module component maps.
conclusions: The induced map $N_1\times_{\varphi_1,M_1}M'_1\to N_2\times_{\varphi_2,M_2}M'_2$ is surjective, with $M_i=M'_i/IM'_i$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjection-module-over-fibre-product}
In Situation \ref{situation-module-over-fibre-product}
let $(N_1, M'_1, \varphi_1) \to (N_2, M'_2, \varphi_2)$ be a morphism
of $\text{Mod}_B \times_{\text{Mod}_A} \text{Mod}_{A'}$
with $N_1 \to N_2$ and $M'_1 \to M'_2$ surjective. Then
$$
N_1 \times_{\varphi_1, M_1} M'_1 \to N_2 \times_{\varphi_2, M_2} M'_2
$$
where $M_1 = M'_1/IM'_1$ and $M_2 = M'_2/IM'_2$ is surjective.

\label{lemma-finite-module-over-fibre-product}
Let $A, A', B, B', I, M, M', N, \varphi$ be as in
Lemma \ref{lemma-module-over-fibre-product}.
If $N$ finite over $B$ and $M'$ finite over $A'$, then
$N' = N \times_{\varphi, M} M'$ is finite over $B'$.

statement:
Let $B\to A$ and $A'\to A$ be ring homomorphisms with $A'\to A$ surjective and kernel $I$. Put $B'=B\times_A A'$.
An object of $\mathrm{Mod}_B\times_{\mathrm{Mod}_A}\mathrm{Mod}_{A'}$ is a triple $(N,M',\varphi)$, where $N$ is a $B$-module, $M'$ is an $A'$-module, and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'\otimes_{A'}A=M'/IM'$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Regard $\varphi$ also as the induced $B$-linear map $N\to M'/IM'$. For such a triple put $M=M'/IM'$ and $N'=N\times_{\varphi,M}M'=\{(n,m')\in N\oplus M':\varphi(n)=m'\pmod{IM'}\}$, with the $B'$-module structure given by the two projections $B'\to B,A'$.
The base-change functor $G:L'\mapsto(L'\otimes_{B'}B,L'\otimes_{B'}A',\mathrm{can})$ defines an equivalence from the category of finite projective $B'$-modules to the full subcategory of compatible triples $(N,M',\varphi)$ in which $N$ is finite projective over $B$ and $M'$ is finite projective over $A'$. Its inverse equivalence is given on objects by $(N,M',\varphi)\mapsto N\times_{\varphi,M}M'$.

conclusions: The indicated base-change functor induces an equivalence between finite projective $B'$-modules and compatible triples with both components finite projective; the fibre-product construction is an inverse equivalence.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-finitely-presented-module-over-fibre-product}
Let $A, A', B, B', I$ be as in
Situation \ref{situation-module-over-fibre-product}.
The category of finite projective $B'$-modules
is equivalent to the full subcategory
of $\text{Mod}_B \times_{\text{Mod}_A} \text{Mod}_{A'}$
consisting of triples $(N, M', \varphi)$
with $N$ finite projective over $B$ and $M'$ finite projective over $A'$.
